get.description: Returns every configuration field of the discovery app, its effective value, and whether an override is in effect.

schema.description: GetInventoryConfigResponse returns the discovery app's configuration.

settings.description: Every field, whether or not it is overridden.

items.description: InventorySetting is one of the discovery app's configuration fields.

key.description: The field name. Nested fields arrive `__`-delimited, e.g. SCHEDULE__every.

default_value.description: What it would be with no override.

type.description: The field's type, for rendering an input.

reload.description: hot when it can be changed at runtime, otherwise it is deployment-only.

has_override.description:
Whether an override is in effect, which is how "why is it set to this" is
answerable without also reading the deployment's configuration file.

is_advanced.description: Whether to hide it behind an "advanced" disclosure.

description.description: The field's documentation, where it has any.

patch.description: Applies a batch of configuration changes atomically: one invalid field rejects the whole batch and writes nothing. Only runtime-changeable fields are accepted.

parameters.description:
The fields to change, as `{key: value}`.

A map of arbitrary JSON rather than named fields, because the app owns which
fields exist and what they are typed as; mirroring them here would mean a proto
change and a `make gen` every time it grows a setting. The app validates and
rejects the batch as a whole.

Bound to the HTTP body directly (`body: "values"`, not `body: "*"`), so the request
this endpoint takes is the same object it forwards. The alternative wraps it as
`{"values": {...}}`, which would make the proxy's shape differ from the shape of the
thing being proxied for no gain to anyone reading either.
parameters.name: values

get.description: Returns every host the discovery app has a row for, whether or not a database was found on it, with the services on each and how current the observations are.

parameters.description:
When set, return only hosts that do (or do not) carry a registered service.
Unset returns both, which is the ordinary listing.
parameters.name: has_service

parameters.description: When true, return only hosts currently failing.
parameters.name: failing

parameters.description: When set, return only hosts served by this Nomad client.
parameters.name: executor

schema.description: ListInventoryHostsResponse returns the hosts POM knows about.

items.description:
InventoryHost is one machine POM knows about, with the services on it.

A host is a row whether or not any MongoDB was found on it. That is what makes
"which machines have no database" a query rather than an absence, and it is the only
way a machine that has never run one appears at all - which is the case installing a
database somewhere later depends on.

node_id.description: PMM's node ID. Also what a scoped refresh is addressed by.

executor_host.description:
The Nomad client that serves it. Unset means nothing can be run there, which is a
fact about the estate rather than a probe failure.

os.description:
The operating system, as the host reports it. Worth having from a probe because
PMM leaves it null for some nodes.

executor.description:
InventoryExecutor reports whether SEP can run anything on a host.

Three flags rather than one, because "orphaned" hid three different problems with
three different fixes: never onboarded (registered false), onboarded and down
(reachable false), and up with a broken raw_exec driver (driver_healthy false). This
is SEP's own knowledge rather than probe output, so it is filled in for every host
on every sweep, including hosts no probe reached.

registered.description: Whether the Tasks backend knows this node at all.

driver_healthy.description: Whether its raw_exec driver is healthy, which is what a probe actually needs.

detail.description: Whatever detail the backend gave, when it gave any.

unregistered_mongods.description: Mongods running that PMM has no service for.

items.description:
UnregisteredMongod is a mongod found running that PMM has no service for.

The arbiter case, mostly: PMM registers no service for an arbiter, so nothing else
in POM would report the process at all. Also what stands in the way of installing
anything over a port that is already taken.

port.description: The port it is listening on.

argv.description: The command line it was started with.

pid.description: Its process ID at the time of the probe.

observed.description:
Everything the probe recorded about the host, including attributes with no field
above.

freshness.description:
InventoryFreshness says how current the rest of a row is, and how it is failing.

Carried on hosts and services alike because the estate is upserted rather than
rebuilt: a row keeps what it last reported, so every attribute is only meaningful
beside the time it was collected. `failing_since` is the *first* failure after the
last success, which is what makes "failing for three days" expressible rather than
only "failed a minute ago".

first_seen_at.description: When POM first wrote a row for this entity.

last_attempt_at.description: When a refresh last tried it.

last_success_at.description:
When it last answered. Unset means it never has, which is different from having
answered nothing.

failing_since.description: The first failure after the last success. Unset means it is not failing.

services.description: The services on it. Empty is a meaningful answer, not a gap.

items.description:
InventoryService is one MongoDB service POM has probed, or tried to.

The typed fields are the ones a table sorts by; `observed` carries the whole
document besides. That split is deliberate: the app stores observations as JSON so
that collecting a new attribute is a payload change rather than a schema change, and
enumerating every attribute here would put that coupling straight back. A new
attribute appears in `observed` the day it is collected and is promoted to a field
of its own only when something wants to sort by it.

get.description: Returns the discovery app's refresh history, newest first. Distinct from /v1/pom/discovery/runs, which is PMM's own collection pass and never probes a host.

parameters.description: How many to return, newest first. Defaults to 20, capped at 100.
parameters.name: limit

schema.description: ListInventoryRunsResponse returns the refresh history, newest first.

items.description: InventoryRun is one refresh of the estate.

finished_at.description: When it stopped. Unset while it is still going.

counts.description: InventoryRunCounts is what one refresh saw.

services_resolved.description: ...of which matched a host something could be run on.

services_orphaned.description: ...of which did not. Not an error.

hosts_total.description:
Hosts in scope this run, service or no service.

A refresh attempts hosts as well as the services on them, so counting only
services makes a refresh of a host with no database read as "0 of 0" - which is
exactly what a run that did nothing looks like, on the one kind of host POM most
exists to describe.

hosts_probeable.description:
...of which had somewhere to run a probe. The gap is the estate nothing can be
dispatched to, which is a fact about onboarding rather than a failed run.

scope.description:
The hosts it was limited to. Empty means it refreshed the whole estate, which is
what the scheduled sweep does.

error.description: What went wrong, when something did.

post.description: Dispatches an on-host probe per executor host and returns as soon as the refresh is accepted. Takes tens of seconds, unlike /v1/pom/discovery/runs. Pass node_ids to refresh only those hosts; 409 when another refresh already holds one of them.

parameters.description: TriggerInventoryRefreshRequest is the request for TriggerInventoryRefresh.
parameters.name: body

schema.description: TriggerInventoryRefreshRequest is the request for TriggerInventoryRefresh.

node_ids.description:
The hosts to refresh, by PMM node ID. Empty refreshes the whole estate.

Plural on purpose: PMM's node ID is also POM's key, so ids pass through
untranslated, and one host is a list of one. A surface taking a single id where
the app takes a list would be a translation step in disguise.

schema.description:
TriggerInventoryRefreshResponse acknowledges an accepted refresh.

Accepted, not finished. A refresh dispatches a Nomad job per host and takes tens of
seconds, unlike PMM's own collection pass, which never probes and completes in
milliseconds. Two triggers that different must not look alike to a caller.

run_id.description: The run's ID, to follow with GetInventoryRun.

scope.description: The hosts it will refresh. Empty means the whole estate.

get.description: Returns one refresh by ID, with what it saw and which hosts it covered.

run.description: InventoryRun is one refresh of the estate.

finished_at.description: When it stopped. Unset while it is still going.

counts.description: InventoryRunCounts is what one refresh saw.

services_resolved.description: ...of which matched a host something could be run on.

services_orphaned.description: ...of which did not. Not an error.

...of which had somewhere to run a probe. The gap is the estate nothing can be
dispatched to, which is a fact about onboarding rather than a failed run.

scope.description:
The hosts it was limited to. Empty means it refreshed the whole estate, which is
what the scheduled sweep does.

error.description: What went wrong, when something did.

entities.description:
What it attempted, one entry per entity.

Only on the detail response, never on the list: a refresh of a real estate has a
row per service, and a history of twenty-five would carry the lot to render a
page that shows one at a time.

items.description:
InventoryRunEntity is one host a refresh attempted, and what came of it.

Host-oriented, because a refresh attempts hosts. A flat list of services - which
this was - cannot show a machine carrying a PMM client and no database, however
many times it is probed, and that machine is the case POM most exists to describe:
it is where a database can be installed.

One dispatch covers every service on a host, so the host owns the timing and the
failure and its services carry only what is theirs. Previously the duration was
copied onto each service, which read as several measurements when it was one.

Deliberately outcomes and not observations. What the probe *found* lives on the
estate, where it is upserted and stays current; a receipt that also carried the
attributes would be a second copy that goes stale the moment the next refresh runs.

node_id.description: PMM's node ID, the key POM holds this host under.

executor_host.description: The client its probe ran on. Unset when none matched.

resolution.description:
name, address or orphaned - how that client was matched, or that it was not.
Orphaned is why nothing ran; it is not an error.

answered.description:
Whether the *host* answered. A different question from whether its services did:
a host with no database answers perfectly well and has no services at all.

duration_seconds.description: The host's wall clock, dispatch to collected output.

error.description: The host-level failure, when its probe failed.

services.description: The services on it. Empty is a meaningful answer, not a gap.

service_id.description: PMM's service ID, when POM could key one.

service_name.description: Its name, so a reader is not left joining UUIDs by hand.

answered.description: Whether the host returned a usable record for it.

error.description: Why it did not, when it did not.

schema.description:
GetTopologyResponse is the whole topology document plus the provenance of the run
behind it.

snapshot.description: Snapshot carries the provenance every snapshot-backed response repeats.

observed_at.description: The newest observation in it, unset when nothing was observed at all.

stale.description: Whether the document is older than the staleness grace period.

run_id.description: The discovery run that produced it.

origin_node.description: The PMM node the document was assembled on.

source_queries.description: The VictoriaMetrics queries the document was derived from.

summary.description: Summary carries the fleet-level counts, so a caller need not re-derive them.

environments.description: The estate, grouped environment then cluster.

env_name.description: Environment label, unset when its services carry none.

items.description: Cluster represents one cluster or replica set.

name.description: Cluster label, unset when its services carry none.

items.description:
Service represents one monitored MongoDB service as the topology document records it.

Two sentinel conventions, and they differ on purpose. cpu_usage_percent and
connections_free_percent are -1 when not measured, never null and never 0, because
zero CPU is a legitimate reading and a numeric column must keep "idle" and "unknown"
apart. replication_lag_seconds and oplog_window_seconds are null when they do not
apply -- a router and a standalone have no replica-set oplog -- which is a different
statement from -1's "we could not measure it".

service_name.description: Service name as PMM inventory registered it.

endpoint.description: host:port as the replica set itself addresses the member.

service_id.description: PMM's service ID. The join key against VictoriaMetrics.

replication_set.description: Replica set, or unset for a router or a standalone.

state.description: PRIMARY, SECONDARY or ARBITER, or unset where there is no replica-set state.

status.description: UP when the exporter reached the service, DOWN when it did not.

cpu_usage_percent.description: CPU percentage, or -1 when not measured.

connections_free_percent.description: Percentage of free connections, or -1 when not measured.

replication_lag_seconds.description: Seconds this member trails the primary; unset where there is no primary to trail.

oplog_window_seconds.description: Seconds of history the oplog holds; unset where there is no replica-set oplog.

installed_version.description:
The MongoDB binary installed on the node, which is not necessarily the one
running. Divergence from `version` is the upgraded-but-not-restarted case. Only
an on-host probe can see it, so this is unset wherever one has not run.

config_path.description: The configuration file the running server read. Probe-only.

argv.description: The command line the running server was started with. Probe-only.
